title: Riyadh Airport Hit Again as US and Allies Warn Travellers Away From Saudi Airports
excerpt: A second strike in two days killed one person at King Khalid International Airport and Dammam's airport was also targeted, as Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis and Western governments tell citizens to avoid Saudi airports.
body:
• King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was attacked for a second consecutive day on Sunday; one person, believed to be a Pakistani resident, was killed and 11 injured.
  • King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also targeted on Sunday evening, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities.
  • The US, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada have warned citizens to avoid Saudi airports; Britain advises against travel to Jeddah and Dammam and all Saudi airports except Medina's.
  • President Trump says he is evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Fourth attack on Riyadh airport in a week

Saudi Arabia's main international airport was attacked again on Sunday, a day after a missile strike on King Khalid International Airport killed at least 13 people and injured more than 300. Sunday's strike hit terminals 3 and 4, killing one person — believed to be a Pakistani resident — and injuring 11, according to reports citing Saudi authorities. The Houthis have now targeted the airport four times in the past week.

https://x.com/JohnBasham/status/2109689084608131217

The attacks widened on Sunday evening, when King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, on the kingdom's eastern coast, was also targeted, with damage assessments under way, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. The Houthis renewed warnings on Sunday urging airlines, airport workers and travellers to avoid Saudi airports, as Saudi Arabia vowed retaliation.

Washington weighs joining the fight

President Donald Trump said he was evaluating whether the United States should join Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. "We may. We're going to look at it," Trump told reporters, according to the Associated Press. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly." Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned Saturday's attack, in which an American citizen was among the dead, calling for an immediate end to the attacks.

The escalation follows a major Saudi-led offensive against the Houthis launched a week ago, after the rebels moved on the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. The US had previously agreed a ceasefire with the Houthis after a month-long bombing campaign, and neither side had appeared eager to resume that conflict — a calculation the airport attacks may now change.

"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."

— President Donald Trump

What this means for Indian travellers

Britain's Foreign Office advises against travel to Jeddah and Dammam and to all Saudi airports except Mohammed bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Medina, and the US and other Western governments have warned citizens to avoid Saudi airports. Indian carriers have already extended cancellations on Saudi routes — see our coverage: Indian Airlines Extend Saudi Flight Cancellations Through October 15. Anyone booked through Riyadh, Jeddah or Dammam in the coming days should confirm flight status with the airline before travelling to the airport and follow the Indian Embassy in Riyadh's advisories. Full reporting on the Sunday strikes is at Fox News and The Times.
